Thanks Priya — quick technical notes that we'll expand into a short doc for the Wednesday deep-dive: 

1) Warm pools & model variant (redwood-open-7b-quant)
- Cold-start for a new worker (container + model load) on our Dedicated tier typically ranges 20-45s depending on instance type and storage layer; quantized 7B reduces load time vs fp16 but still non-trivial.
- Warm pool (pre-loaded model instances) can achieve first-token times under 200ms for short prompts because KV cache is already initialized. For your sub-10s cold-start requirement, we recommend a hybrid warm-pool + proactive pre-warm strategy around anticipated windows (based on your traffic signals) — this gives near-instant behavior for the bulk of requests and keeps autoscale headroom for unexpected spikes.

2) Scale-up timelines & burst handling
- Autoscaler ramp (spin up new instances from zero): ~60-120s typical; with GRACEFUL_WARM settings and image pre-pulling we can get to ~40-90s.
- Warm-pool-enabled ramp: if warm pool size is tuned to cover expected baseline bursts, user-visible latency stays within SLO while autoscaler adds capacity in background.
- When max capacity is reached, our runtime supports two fallback behaviors configurable per route: (a) queue with configurable max wait (we can set 10s for UI-critical); (b) graceful degradation to a smaller/cheaper model variant with identical interface (e.g., redwood-open-3b-quant) — we can instrument confidence checks to ensure quality.

3) Queueing and backpressure
- For UI-critical routes we recommend low queue limits (<=10s) and prefer fallback to pre-warmed smaller variant rather than long queues.
- For background jobs, queueing up to 30s is acceptable and more cost-efficient.

4) Batching and KV cache tuning
- Continuous batching helps throughput but increases P99 latency if not bounded; we will propose batch size caps per route based on your token distribution.
- KV cache lifetime and sharing strategy (per-session vs per-user) will have big impact on first-token times for multi-turn chat; we will model that in the perf test.

I'll put these points into a short technical note and drop the numbers into the capacity-plan spreadsheet Marissa attached.
